skill.displayName: Frog Skin Moisture Assessment | 蛙类皮肤湿润度评估

llm.summary: This skill is a cloud-based frog media analysis tool, but it needs Review because it automatically links a user identity, uploads media, queries cloud history, and stores account tokens locally.

dimensions.detail: The runtime reads OpenClaw identity environment variables and workspace data/smyx-api-key.txt, accepts local paths or URLs, uploads supplied local file contents, and sends requests to remote services. This is partly expected for cloud analysis, but the credential and identity handling is broader than a simple image-assessment skill.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: No destructive install hook or background worker was found. The artifact ships Python scripts plus requests, SQLAlchemy, and YAML dependencies, and relies on configured external lifeemergence.com/open.lifeemergence.com services.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill instructs automatic triggering for frog media and history-report keywords, requires cloud history lookup, and tells the agent not to ask for or expose internal identity values. That gives users limited runtime control over identity-linked cloud access.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The code creates a workspace data directory and SQLite database, auto-creates or reuses a default user, silently logs in/registers against a remote endpoint, and stores token/openToken values in the local sys_user table.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The main frog skin moisture workflow is coherent with media upload, remote analysis, and report retrieval, and those are largely disclosed in SKILL.md. However, the package also includes generic HTTP/CRUD helpers, user lookup/account code, a generic video-analysis entry point, and local token-bearing user persistence that are broader than the narrow frog assessment purpose.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Review before installing. Use this only if you are comfortable sending frog images/videos or supplied URLs to the configured cloud service and having reports associated with an internal identity. Avoid sensitive local files or private/internal URLs, and be aware it may create a local workspace database containing reusable service tokens.
llm.findings:
[AST7] unexpected: The dynamic getattr use in the generic DAO is real, but it is an internal ORM helper rather than the main user-facing capability; it is a supporting code-quality/privacy concern, not evidence of command execution.
[LP3] unexpected: The skill documentation discloses file handling, remote API use, history lookup, and identity handling, but there is no separate least-privilege manifest declaring those capabilities.
[TP4] unexpected: Remote media analysis and cloud reports are disclosed and aligned with the stated service, but generic platform APIs, account management, and token persistence go beyond the narrow frog skin assessment framing.
[SDI-1] unexpected: History listing is disclosed in SKILL.md and can support reports, but the package also includes generic analysis/API components and broad CRUD-style helpers not tightly scoped to frog moisture analysis.
[SDI-2] unexpected: The hidden open-id flow, workspace api-key read, auto default-user creation, remote phoneLogin/register call, and local token storage are artifact-backed and materially under user-directed control.
[SDI-4] unexpected: The generic smyx_analysis CLI still describes itself as video analysis; this appears to be shared scaffolding and is less severe than the identity/persistence issues, but it does show packaging scope drift.
[SQP-1] expected: Automatic invocation for frog media and report keywords is documented, but the history-query trigger is broad and directly calls the cloud report API without an explicit confirmation step.
[SQP-2] expected: Uploading provided media to a backend is expected for this cloud analysis design, but the artifact does not require a clear runtime confirmation before transmitting local files, URLs, identity fields, and authorization tokens.
[E1] unexpected: The requests.post to /sys/phoneLogin with silent registration and openId/mobile fields is real and is the strongest concern because it creates or links an account outside the core visual assessment task.
[YR4] unexpected: A hidden-character check found a single zero-width joiner in an emoji line; I did not find prompt override text or deceptive hidden instructions, so this was downgraded.
